data.ideal_summary: We performed ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and parallel RNA-seq on human or mouse cells treated with an mTOR inhibitor (Torin1, rapamycin or INK128/sapanisertib) or vehicle control to measure genome-wide changes in translation. Matched ribosome-protected fragment and total mRNA libraries were prepared from the same samples to calculate translation efficiency. Differential translation analysis identified mRNAs, such as TOP and TOP-like mRNAs, whose translation efficiency changed after mTOR inhibition.
method_notes: Translation efficiency needs Ribo-seq and RNA-seq from the same samples and conditions; Ribo-seq alone only gives ribosome occupancy, not efficiency.
Rapamycin is a partial mTORC1 inhibitor, whereas Torin1 and INK128 are ATP-competitive and strongly suppress 4E-BP-dependent translation, so effect sizes differ.
Polysome profiling or TMT proteomics can be alternatives if Ribo-seq is lacking, but they do not measure translation at codon resolution.
